attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own article, endorsed.

semantics.note: The normalised text keeps 'was and is' for the GAMA CEO role, the co-founder role, the 'purportedly' qualifier and the claim that the two companies are the same. It is a factual observation.

contract.note: Zitron himself wrote 'was and is', so requiring the CEO role to continue as of May 6, 2024 is a plain reading. Reading 'same company' as one legal entity that changed its name is the ordinary sense. Treating a retrospective denial as inconclusive is fair.

evidence.note: In a Feb 2022 interview, a GAMA team representative calls Lyu 'our CEO'. This supports the past CEO role only. It is a company-side statement.
Rabbit's January 2024 launch release names Lyu as founder and CEO and introduces the R1 as an AI device. This supports the founder and product parts. It is a company disclosure.

Cointelegraph (May 24, 2024) reports Rabbit's own statement that Rabbit was rebranded from Cyber Manufacture, with GAMA as a separate venture under the same company. This supports corporate continuity, but it relies on the company's word rather than the filing.

Rabbit says in hindsight that GAMA ended when it was open-sourced. That challenges the claim that Lyu still led it, but it gives no dated departure and is an unsupported company denial, so it does not settle the point.

reviews.rationale: Some parts are supported: Lyu's past GAMA CEO role (e1), his founding of Rabbit and its R1 device (e2), and the Cyber Manufacture-to-Rabbit rebrand (e3, based on Rabbit's own statement). Nothing in the packet shows whether Lyu was still GAMA's CEO on May 6, 2024. Rabbit's after-the-fact closure claim (e4) is not a reliable record that the role ended. The contract requires every part to be shown, so the whole claim stays unresolved.
